## Pick a Project

Here's my CEP case study, the Case 31 dashboard, and the styling page.
The case study is still in progress. The dashboard uses separate teaching data.

::: {#portfolio-examples}
:::

## What Does a Listing Do?

A listing collects links and descriptions into one place. Quarto can read
that information from pages or from a YAML file. I used `projects.yml` for
this site because there are only three entries to keep track of.

When I add a project to that file and render again, Quarto adds it to the
table. I still need to publish the updated site for visitors to see it.

## The Settings I Used

These are the main settings in this page's header:

```yaml
listing:
  id: portfolio-examples
  contents: projects.yml
  type: table
  fields: [title, description, categories]
  sort: "title"
  categories: true
```

`contents` points to my entries. `type` chooses the layout, and `fields`
chooses the columns. I also renamed the column headings in the full header
and turned off the search and sorting controls for this small collection.

The div named `portfolio-examples` puts the listing just below my introduction.

## Add a Project

Here's the dashboard entry from `projects.yml`:

```yaml
- title: "Case 31: Credit Union Member Experience"
  path: case31-dashboard.html
  description: "Employee ratings, service awareness, and loan perceptions from the Case 31 teaching data."
  categories: [R, Survey Analysis, Quarto]
```

The `path` is the page that opens when someone clicks the title.
Categories let visitors browse by skill. For example, choosing **R**
shows the dashboard entry.

## Why I Chose a Table

| Layout | Where I'd use it |
|---|---|
| `table` | A short list of projects that are easy to compare |
| `grid` | Projects with useful preview images |
| `default` | Blog posts or entries with longer descriptions |

A table works for these three examples. If I add projects with preview
images later, I'd try a grid.
